segments.he: גְּמָ׳ תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן. לָשָׁה, הִיא מְקַטֶּפֶת, וַחֲבֶירְתָּהּ לָשָׁה תַּחְתֶּיהָ. מְקַטֶּפֶת, הִיא אוֹפָה, וַחֲבֶירְתָּהּ מְקַטֶּפֶת תַּחְתֶּיהָ, וְהַשְּׁלִישִׁית לָשָׁה. אוֹפָה הִיא, לָשָׁה, וַחֲבֶירְתָּהּ אוֹפָה תַּחְתֶּיהָ, וְהַשְּׁלִישִׁית מְקַטֶּפֶת, וְחוֹזְרֹת חֲלִילָה. כׇּל זְמַן שֶׁעוֹסְקוֹת בַּבָּצֵק — אֵינוֹ בָּא לִידֵי חִימּוּץ.
segments.en: «GEMARA:» «The Sages taught» in a baraita: When the woman who «kneads» first completes her kneading, «she arranges» her dough «and another» woman «kneads in her place.» When the first woman finishes «arranging» her dough, «she bakes and another» woman «arranges» her dough «in her place, and the third» woman «kneads» her dough. When the first woman finishes «baking, she kneads» the dough for her next batch, «and another» woman «bakes in her place, and the third» woman «arranges» her dough, «and they continue in turn. As long as they are engaged» in handling «the dough, it will not become leavened.»

moves.summary: the baraita explains the Rabbis' staggered procedure in the mishna

edges.about: the baraita spells out the rotating order of kneading, arranging and baking behind the Rabbis' ruling in the mishna

positions.claim: as long as the women keep working the dough it does not leaven

unresolved.issue: the link of the baraita to the Rabbis of the mishna is stated only in Steinsaltz's gloss, not in the Talmud text; interprets edge marked inferred
